newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda coffee trade looks for higher quality crops.
newsitem.headline: Uganda coffee trade looks for higher quality crops.

text.p: The exporter-based Uganda Coffee Trade Federation (UCTF) sees a shift to production of higher quality coffees as a solution to problems posed by falling world prices.
Executive Director Frederick Kawuma said, "Trade has not been very good with prices in a space of four months steadily dropping from over $1,650 per tonne to under $1,300 per tonne."

However, he added, "Once we have good consistent quality, our producers can reap huge benefits in the market. We can and are entering the gourmet sector, where already promising contacts have been made.
"Our members can begin selling their coffee at higher prices, where premiums are offered for superior qualities."
As one step of improving coffee quality, Kawuma said the UCTF had put in place a code of conduct through which "many malpractices will be phased out of the coffee sector".

Kawuma said Ugandan exporters planned to participate in coffee fairs in Vienna in June and London in October as part of efforts to raise their market share. They would also participate at a conference in New Orleans, Florida, in April.
"We hope our members will be more actively involved in presenting this coffee at international coffee fairs," he said.

Kawuma saw the recent appointment of Uganda's minister of state for trade and industry as vice-chairman of a task force for African producers as helpful in securing support from other producers on mechanisms to bolster prices.

The minister, Abel Rwendeire, is in Vietman with officials from other countries which want Vietnam to join the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) in order to strengthen any initiatives the ACPC might take.
In Uganda the exporters federation has also completed a draft of the rules and procedures for arbitration within the internal marketing system geared towards improving domestic trade.
Kawuma listed other plans for Uganda's coffee market as improved information flows between buyers and their agents, exporters and the federation secretariat.
